summary: Round 4 introduces the agentic-seo-loop skill: a repeatable, resumable pipeline that measures the site's SEO state, harvests Semrush keyword data (US), asks an LLM (Gemini 2.5 Flash by default, Gemma-4-31b-it as an emergency fallback) for per-page copy proposals, applies deterministic perf/CWV fixes, patches non-CMS pages, and re-audits the whole thing on a staged branch. This pass shipped the full framework (15 skill files: SKILL.md, config, 5 worker scripts, 5 shared libs, 3 references) plus ONE real code change — postdetail-h1-demote — which reduced the multi-h1 offender count from 1 to 0. The loop generated one high-confidence copy proposal for /technology/spacy (vol=390, KD=35%) which was correctly classified as CMS-owned and handed off to the operator instead of being force-merged. See notes about Google free-tier daily quota exhaustion (20 req/day/model) and the small editable code surface (~18 top-level static pages; most of jedi-v2 is Hygraph-driven).

layout.SKILL.md: Skill entrypoint — when to use, requirements, artifacts, rollback, known limitations
layout.config/jedi-v2.yaml: Site-specific policy: editable routes, CMS-owned prefixes, keyword/matching/api thresholds, worker layout
layout.scripts/orchestrator.mjs: w0 — cuts agent/round4-<utc-ts> branch, syncs skill into repo, snapshots audit-before, dispatches analyst then w2/w3/w4 in parallel, rebuilds + audits, commits with a truthful auto-generated message
layout.scripts/analyst.mjs: w1 — auto-seed extraction, Semrush harvest (US, cached), page match, LLM per-candidate edit + new-page proposals
layout.scripts/perf-fixer.mjs: w2 — deterministic non-LLM fixes; ships one real fix (postdetail-h1-demote), sentinel-guarded and idempotent
layout.scripts/content-injector.mjs: w3 — patches <SEO> string-literal attrs + <h1> on editable routes; hands off CMS-owned proposals to operator
layout.scripts/page-scaffolder.mjs: w4 — creates new /topics/<slug>/index.jsx, wires App.jsx + enumerate-routes.mjs + generate-sitemap.js. Zero pages scaffolded this pass (no whitespace opportunities in filtered seeds)
layout.scripts/lib/semrush.mjs: Keyword Magic Tool RapidAPI client. Handles vendor typo 'searche volume' (parsed as integer), '1.9k'/'50'/'0' volume strings, '76%' KD strings. SHA1-cached on shared workspace, 1 req/sec rate limit, 30s backoff on 429
layout.scripts/lib/gemma.mjs: Google Generative Language client. Default model gemini-2.5-flash; fallback chain gemini-2.5-flash-lite -> gemini-2.0-flash -> gemma-4-31b-it. 65s backoff on 429, 3 retries per model. Auto-strips thinkingConfig on 400 'not supported'. buildEditPrompt + buildNewPagePrompt helpers.
layout.scripts/lib/seed-extractor.mjs: cheerio-based dist walker. Extracts title/H1/JSON-LD name. Strips brand suffix, splits on connectors, filters noise (pure brand, 2-token names, 404 prerenders, short/long, common noise words)
layout.scripts/lib/page-matcher.mjs: Fuzzy match: exact substring (score 1.0), token Jaccard (0.0-0.95), slug bonus (+0.15). Thresholds edit>=0.6, new<=0.4, skip 0.4-0.6
layout.references/gemma-prompt-templates.md: Exact prompts used, tuneable for prompt engineering
layout.references/troubleshooting.md: Common failure modes: quota exhaustion, EPERM on empty JSONL, cheerio module resolution, Chrome missing

postdetail_h1_demote.change: Demoted the first <h1> in the Hygraph rich-text renderer to <h2>. The blog post detail page renders both an outer title <h1> (from the page component) and a rich-text heading-one <h1> block, tripping the multi-h1-per-page audit warn. The outer title is the correct primary h1; the inner one is CMS content that should be a subheading.

loop_state_this_pass.seed_note: 60 -> 40 after cap. Also filtered: 3 stale 404 prerenders (from previous rounds' orphaned use-case sub-routes) and 5-7 team-member 2-token name patterns.

llm_proposals.note: This pass generated 0 organic proposals because Google's free-tier daily quota (20 req/day/model) was exhausted by earlier smoke tests + orchestrator runs during the session. The one CMS-handoff proposal shown above is from run round4-2026-07-07T1808 where quota was still available.

semrush_keyword_magic_tool.notes: Vendor rate limits aggressively when querying novel keywords. Cache hits do NOT count against rate limit.

gemma-4-26b-a4b-it.notes: Model burns 300-800 tokens on internal thinking before emitting text; often returns finishReason=MAX_TOKENS with empty content

gemma-4-31b-it.notes: Ignores 'return only JSON' instructions; echoes reasoning verbatim. Unusable for structured extraction with current prompts.

known_limitations: Editable code surface is thin: ~18 top-level static pages have real .jsx files; everything under /blog/*, /technology/*, /solutions/*, /use-cases/*, /methodology/*, /industries/*, /team/*, /careers/*, /case-studies/*, /ai-training/* is Hygraph-driven. Proposals for those routes are handed off via cms-proposals-not-applied.jsonl.

Gemini free-tier daily quota is 20 requests per day per model. After ~40-60 seeds, the loop will exhaust primary + fallbacks. Reset happens at midnight PT. To keep the loop running through a full session, either budget for a paid API tier or shard seeds across days.
Gemma 4 models (26b-a4b-it, 31b-it) do not reliably emit clean JSON. Kept in the fallback chain but expect degraded quality vs Gemini.

Semrush no-data on very-long-tail queries (>~50 chars) is common. The seed-extractor is intentionally biased toward the site's existing vocabulary, which includes some very-long-tail phrases pulled from H1s.
String-literal attributes only: the content injector rewrites <SEO title="..." description="..."> when both are string literals. Dynamic JSX values ({foo}) are left alone.
US-only Semrush: the vendor supports many countries but this pass only queries US. Non-US markets are cached in the raw payload.

round_5_cms_workflow.note: Since ~80% of the site's SEO surface lives in Hygraph, build a companion 'cms-seo-loop' skill that reads cms-proposals-not-applied.jsonl and (a) generates a PR-comment or PR checklist, (b) if the Hygraph management API is available, drafts CMS updates via GraphQL mutations for operator approval. Without this, the current loop's LLM proposals for CMS-owned routes are a dead-letter queue.

round_5_paid_llm_tier.note: Move off Google free-tier. Options: (a) Vertex AI paid tier with same key (higher rate limits), (b) Anthropic Claude Sonnet ($3/million input) — better JSON compliance than Gemma, (c) Together AI or Fireworks-hosted open models for cost. Current per-pass token budget is ~100k input + ~15k output tokens => under $1 at commercial rates.

round_5_semrush_paid_or_alt.note: RapidAPI Semrush endpoint has aggressive 429s. Consider (a) Semrush direct API (rate limit 10 req/sec commercial), (b) Ahrefs Keyword Explorer API (better long-tail data), (c) DataForSEO (aggregates multiple vendors). Alternatively narrow the seed universe — this pass wasted 12/40 requests on no-data long-tail phrases.

round_5_seed_quality.note: Current seed-extractor pulls from titles/H1s. Many of those are already very-long-tail (>50 chars). Add a step that extracts noun phrases from body copy (n-grams filtered by frequency + stopwords) to seed with mid-tail terms that vendors actually have data for.

round_5_perf_fixer_scope.note: Current perf-fixer only ships one fix. Add real, verified fixes as they're identified: e.g. font-preload hints, above-the-fold LCP image explicit dimensions if any HERO components lack them, specific route-level lazy imports.
